### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3fb90bc253bd04a93b642aecd72244baec7f523d` — the merge of head `bb8c665baa276edfac440fcd1630700e19c8e2e8` into base `4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3fb90bc253bd04a93b642aecd72244baec7f523d && git checkout 3fb90bc253bd04a93b642aecd72244baec7f523d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc bb8c665baa276edfac440fcd1630700e19c8e2e8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc && git merge --no-ff bb8c665baa276edfac440fcd1630700e19c8e2e8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`git diff --stat` of `api-surface/` base..head empty), `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (`ui/ActionButtonProps` sites `""` and `onSuccess`, unchanged), `validate-component-props.ts` L146-198 and L395-445 (`ComponentPropsMap` dispatch, `safeParse`, issue path joined under `properties`), `validate-action-copy-templates.test.ts` L125-131, the four action renderers' `paramsPayload` and `confirmText` forwards (`action-button.tsx` L256-258/L333, `action-icon.tsx` L154-156/L199, `action-group.tsx` L350-352/L380, `action-menu.tsx` L273-275/L312), `ActionRunner.ts` L1657-1680 (confirm awaited, then `actionParams` read and the param dialog opened), `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header and level axis, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`CATEGORIES` L554-557, `findMigrationPrescription` L1900, the signal readers L710-718), `pr-automation.yml` L1001-1002 and L1152 (the Check Changeset job runs both checkers), `lint.yml` (which Type Check lane runs `check:docs` / `check:authorable-surface` and which runs `check:api-surface`), `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` L22, AGENTS.md § Touched `packages/spec`, Prime Directive #14, Post-Task Checklist rule 3, and the precedent review 6597260383 on PR #29829. A read-only census of the head tree: every file under `examples/`, `packages/`, `ui/`, `skills/`, `apps/`, `content/`, `docs/`, `templates` naming `action:button` (CHANGELOG excluded), 45-line window after each occurrence, kept when it holds `confirmText` and `params: [`. The face: `--paths` on the six files returns `hits` = `action-confirm-beside-params.ts`, `action.zod.ts`, `component.zod.ts` (published schema sources); the PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the narrowing face applies and the tier is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER either way.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept-set change the diff implies is exactly one refusal, on one door, for one shape.** `ActionButtonPropsSchema` gains one `.refine(...)` at the end of its chain, after its four `superRefine`s, whose predicate is the negation of `declaresConfirmBesideParams(data)` and whose issue is `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL`. The predicate reads: `confirmText` is neither `null` nor `undefined`, and `params` is an array whose length is at least one. On this row `params` is `z.unknown()`, so the three shapes the ruling distinguishes resolve as: no `params` (undefined, not an array) accepted; `params: []` (length 0) accepted; object-form `params` (not an array) accepted; an array of length at least one beside a declared `confirmText` refused at path `['confirmText']`, `code: 'custom'`. That is the ruling's scope exactly, with no narrower predicate needed. Right.
2. **Same message, same path, as the other two doors.** The refusal object is the one `ActionSchema` and `InlineActionSchema` read; the test pins the button issue's message equal to both with `toBe`. One predicate, one wording, three doors. Right.
3. **`ActionSchema` and `InlineActionSchema` behave exactly as on `main`.** The non-comment code diff of `action.zod.ts` is one added import line and the deletion of the module-private function and object; both refine call sites (`ActionSchema` L2312-2313, `InlineActionSchema` L2627-2628) are untouched and now bind the same names from `./action-confirm-beside-params`. The function body and the message string in the new module are byte-identical to the deleted ones (compared in the diff). The new module imports nothing, so no cycle is introduced. Right.
4. **The module stays internal.** No `index.ts` under `packages/spec/src` names `action-confirm-beside-params`; `ui/index.ts` re-exports `action.zod` with `export *`, which is exactly why the names could not be exported from there without publishing them. The three sibling internal modules the PR cites as the pattern (`action-on-success-executor.ts`, `action-declarative-update.ts`, `list-view-export-options.ts`) are likewise absent from every barrel and from `api-surface/ui.json`, as are `declaresConfirmBesideParams` and `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL`. `git diff --stat bb2c04e3 bb8c665b -- packages/spec/api-surface` is empty. The npm tarball's `files` carries `src/**/*.zod.ts`, which the new `.ts` module is not in; it ships compiled inside `dist` through the importers, as its three siblings do. The public surface does not move. Right.
5. **The deviation is the right placement.** The card wrote "reuse `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL` / `declaresConfirmBesideParams` from `action.zod.ts` after #29829, or its equivalent". Exporting them from `action.zod.ts` would have published two helpers as package API through the `export *` barrel, moved `api-surface/ui.json`, and made the refusal's wording a public contract for no consumer; an internal sibling module reaches the same reuse with none of that cost and follows a pattern already in the tree. A deviation in placement, declared in the dev report and the PR body, not in behaviour. Right.
6. **The describe change is true where it renders, and only there.** The button row's own `confirmText` describe appends the refusal sentence; `ACTION_ROW_COPY_DESCRIBE.confirmText`, shared with `action:icon` and the group/menu members, is untouched, which is correct because those rows do not refuse the pair. `ActionButtonPropsSchema` renders on one reference page (`content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`); the regenerated row carries the new sentence verbatim and nothing else moved in that file. `Type Check · source gates`, the lane that runs `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface`, concluded `success`. Right.
7. **No authorable key moves; no ledger moves.** No key is added, removed or renamed; `authorable-surface/` is untouched. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` already lists the root site `""` for `ui/ActionButtonProps`, so a further root-level `.refine` needs no ledger entry, and the file is unchanged in the diff. Right.
8. **The measurement grounding the ruling holds in the cited code.** `action-button.tsx` L256-258 forwards an array `params` as `actionParams` and an object `params` only as static `params` (read through `readStaticParamValues`), and L333 forwards `confirmText`; `ActionRunner.execute` L1657-1663 awaits the confirm, then L1675-1680 reads `actionParams` (or an array `params`) and opens the param dialog when its length is positive. Two dialogs, in that order, for exactly the shape the predicate refuses; an object `params` reaches the runner as values and opens none. Right.
9. **The door is real.** `validate-component-props.ts` dispatches each page component's `properties` to `ComponentPropsMap[type].safeParse` (L198, L427) and reports each issue at `${path}.properties.${issue.path}` under `component-props-invalid`, so the refusal lands at `pages[N].regions[N].components[N].properties.confirmText` on every CLI command and the runtime `page` save. Right.
10. **Test shape.** Five tests: the refusal (path, code, message equal to both other doors) and four accept controls (`description` beside an array, no `params`, `params: []`, object `params`). The dev dropped a locale-map case after its first ablation showed it vacuous (the row's template slot refuses a locale map for its own reason), which is the honest shape. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29844-action-button-confirm-beside-params-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed (...)`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the `fix(spec)!:` summary, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) ...` marker. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. The only package the diff moves is `@objectstack/spec`. Under the level checker's level axis (`narrowed` ⇒ at least one moved package `minor` or above; the `(narrowing)` arm beside `narrowed` is the required pairing; breaking ships `minor` during the launch window), `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is the level the rule prescribes. The `Check Changeset` run on the head, which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base`, concluded `success`, so the marker parsed, the category is in `CATEGORIES`, and `findMigrationPrescription` found no prescription in the body's "The remedy" paragraph.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind: "a value refused ... a requirement tightened" is AGENTS.md's definition, and a page `action:button` may no longer carry `confirmText` beside a non-empty array `params`.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no key added, removed or renamed; the census (mine, on the head tree, agrees with the dev's at the base) finds 0 shipped carriers and one lint test fixture (`validate-action-copy-templates.test.ts` L131) that feeds the copy-template rule, which never parses `ActionButtonPropsSchema`; the one rewrite there could be needs the author to read the sentence. The sibling precedent #29829 carries the same marker for the same case. No `docs/adr/**` path is touched, which is also the only Tier S shape this PR could land in. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev deviation: predicate and refusal relocated to an internal module instead of exported from `action.zod.ts`.** Judged in ① 4-5: the module is not re-exported from any barrel, `api-surface/` is unchanged, both action doors are byte-for-byte the same behaviour, and the placement follows three siblings already in the tree. Answered: holds, and it is the better placement.
2. **Dev finding, same family outside the ruling: `action:icon` and the `action:group` / `action:menu` members accept the pair.** Confirmed true in the cited code. `ActionIconPropsSchema` (L4093) and `actionContainerMemberShape` (L4243) both declare `confirmText` through `actionRowCopy` and `params: z.unknown()`, and their chains end at `refuseRowOnSuccessBesideExecutor` with no pair rule. Their renderers forward exactly as the button does: `action-icon.tsx` L154-156 (`Array.isArray(schema.params) ? { actionParams: schema.params, params: staticValues } : ...`) and L199 (`confirmText`); `action-group.tsx` L350-352 and L380; `action-menu.tsx` L273-275 and L312; all three hand the result to the same `ActionRunner`, so the same two dialogs open. On a group/menu member a non-array `params` is already refused on every non-`api` type, so the only pair left there is precisely the two-dialog one. Ruling 6597621758 names `ActionButtonPropsSchema` only, and the PR claims nothing about these rows (the shared describe is deliberately unchanged, the changeset says so). Escalated to the seat as a candidate decision card (one A/B question covering the three rows), not a must-fix on this PR.
3. **Dev deviations "harness assignee/reviewer step skipped" and "commit trailers model-free".** Both are standing rules (os-dev rule 2; AGENTS.md's model-free trailer pair), not deviations from this card. Answered: no action.
4. **`open_questions` on 6599345445:** none. Answered.
5. **The branch is behind `main`, merge-tree clean, not merged.** At review time 14 commits behind (the dev reported 10; four more landed since). Of the 14, none touches any of the six PR paths; under `packages/spec` only `api-surface/data.json` and `api-surface/system.json` moved, neither in this diff. A local `merge-tree --write-tree` against `origin/main` writes a tree with no conflict; GitHub reports `mergeable: true` (`mergeable_state: blocked`, the draft and the running checks). The queue rebuilds on `main` and reruns the spec gates there. AGENTS.md § Multi-agent 10 asks for a `main` merge only on a conflict, a `main`-caused red or a queue removal, so not merging is the rule, not a deviation. Answered: does not matter.
6. **Check-runs on `bb8c665b` at review time (63 runs on the second read).** Concluded `success`: Auto Label, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates (carries `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface`), filter. `skipped`: 18.x upgrade harness, Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. Still `in_progress` with no conclusion: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates (carries `check:api-surface`), Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. Reported as seen, not waited for; the queue guard reads the required set before landing. The PR body's local readings (spec 806 files / 24050 tests, lint 215, ui 278, dogfood 3359, 102 derived gate families) are the dev's account and are not adopted here.
7. **Governed surfaces:** none of the six paths is under `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/workflows/**`; the Governed Surface Queue Guard concluded `success`. Tier S landing on this record.
8. **Prose that names fewer doors than now refuse.** `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` L22 ("A registered action is refused it beside a non-empty `params`") stays a true sentence and names the remedy; it is a Tier H path and outside this PR. The seat may fold it into the follow-up in 2. Answered.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/action-confirm-beside-params.ts` — holds.** Judged against the two doors it was lifted from on `main` and the third it now serves. The function body and the message are byte-identical to the module-private originals; the module has no imports, so it cannot cycle with `action.zod.ts` or `component.zod.ts`; it is exported from no barrel and absent from `api-surface/`. Its docblock names the three doors, the runner order it rests on, and why an empty or object `params` is not the pair. Attempts to break it: (a) a consumer importing it by deep path is not possible through `package.json` `exports`, which list only the subpath barrels; (b) the `files` glob `src/**/*.zod.ts` excludes it from the shipped source, as it excludes its three siblings, and the compiled `dist` carries it through its importers. Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.

**`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` — holds.** Judged against the published spec on `main`: the diff is one import and the deletion of the two module-private definitions, plus comment text; both refine call sites are unchanged and bind the same values. `ActionSchema` and `InlineActionSchema` accept and refuse exactly what they did on `main`, and the existing sixteen guard-test cases on those doors still pin that. No export added or removed. Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.

**`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` — holds.** Judged against ruling 6597621758 letter A and its first consumers (lint `validateComponentProps` at the CLI and runtime `page` doors; the `action:button` renderer through `ActionRunner`).
- *Does it make the spec's own refusal real at the consumer?* Yes. The gate parses the row through `ComponentPropsMap`, and the issue lands at `properties.confirmText` with the action doors' message naming the `description` remedy, which the row declares and the renderer forwards to the param dialog.
- *Does it take a declared capability away beyond the ruling?* No. With `params: z.unknown()`, the `Array.isArray` test joined with a positive-length test is the complete reading of "non-empty array": an object (static values, no dialog), an empty array and an absent `params` all parse, as the four controls pin. A blank `confirmText` (`''`) is `!= null` and is refused beside an array, which is how both other doors read it on `main`; a locale-map `confirmText` is refused by the row's template slot before the predicate matters.
- *Attempts to break it.* (a) The `strictObject` alias layer (`ACTION_NODE_ALIASES`) renames `endpoint` and friends, never `params` or `confirmText`, so the predicate sees the authored pair. (b) Zod 4 runs every `.refine` on the chain, so the four `superRefine`s still report on the same body; the test reads the issue by path, not index. (c) The refine adds no key, so `check:authorable-surface` has nothing to move (its lane concluded `success`); it changes the schema's type not at all, so `ActionButtonProps` / `ActionButtonPropsParsed` and their ui readers (`runner-variant.ts`, `public-blocks.zod.ts`) are unaffected. (d) `action:bar` spreads a registered action onto an `action:button` node; that member is an `ActionSchema`, which already refuses the pair, so no previously-valid composition is newly refused there. (e) The describe change touches only this row's `confirmText`, so the shared describe on `action:icon` and the members stays true for rows that do not refuse the pair.
- *Must-fix:* none.
- *Should-fix:* none on the hits files. For the seat's follow-up list only: the `action:icon` / `action:group` / `action:menu` pair in ③ 2, and the skills prose line in ③ 8.
